title: Weather and Climate
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Temperature falls about 6.5 degrees Celsius per 1000 metres. Climate change: rising temperatures, unreliable rain, longer droughts, heavier floods; responses include tree planting, water harvesting and drought-resistant crops.

skills.key_step: The child names the factors that influence climate in Africa and describes its major climatic regions.

floor.prerequisite: Describes the climatic regions of Eastern Africa.
floor.question: Describe the equatorial climate.

board.do: Draw a mountain 3000 metres high, 25 degrees at the bottom.

board.say: About how cold is the top?

misconceptions.ask: What happens to temperature as you climb a mountain?
misconceptions.repair: Think of the snow on Mount Kenya at the equator.

misconceptions.ask: Which climate has hot, wet weather all year?
misconceptions.repair: Link the Congo basin with rain every day.

misconceptions.ask: How can a cold ocean current affect a coast?
misconceptions.repair: Use the Namib desert next to the cold Benguela current (to confirm).

checks.question: Give three factors that influence climate.
checks.answer: any three of: latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, winds, relief

checks.question: What happens to temperature as you climb?

skills.key_step: The child says what climate change is, its causes and effects on the environment and people, and picks ways to address it.

floor.prerequisite: Says how weather matters to people.
floor.question: Give one way weather affects farming.
floor.answer: planting and harvest depend on rain

steps: Name effects on land and people.
contexts: tree planting on a national tree day

board.do: Draw a line rising slowly over many years.

board.say: Is this one day's weather or a change in climate?

board.do: Write two causes and two responses.

misconceptions.ask: Is one very hot day proof of climate change?
misconceptions.repair: Show a temperature line over 50 years, not one day.

misconceptions.ask: Which action can make climate change worse?
misconceptions.repair: Show trees taking in carbon dioxide.

misconceptions.ask: How can unreliable rain affect farmers?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to maize when the rains fail.

misconceptions.ask: Give one thing a learner can do about climate change.
misconceptions.repair: List small actions and add up a whole school doing them.

checks.question: Give one effect of climate change on people.
checks.answer: any of: crop failure, loss of pasture, floods, water shortage, disease

checks.question: Give one way to address climate change.
checks.answer: any of: planting trees, saving energy, water harvesting, drought-resistant crops, early warning
